Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "topology", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "For each \(x\in[0,1)\), we have \(x^n\to0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
Any uniform limit would necessarily equal this pointwise limit. Fix \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12\). For every \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), let \(n=N\) and \(x=2^{-1/N}\). Then \(x<1\), so \(f(x)=0\), whereas
\[
|f_n(x)-f(x)|=x^N=\frac12.
\]
Hence for every \(N\) there exist \(n\ge N\) and \(x\in[0,1]\) such that \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\tfrac12\). Therefore \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\)."}
